note: DECLARED, NOT PROVEN — and therefore not launchable. The Codex CLI is not installed on deployment #0 (verified 2026-08-13 by worker-harness-core and again 2026-08-14: `command -v codex` finds nothing, no ~/.codex, no ~/.config/codex). Every mechanism below is written from the vendor's documented interface and NONE has been probed against a running binary, so `status` stays `declared` and every route naming this descriptor refuses at preflight with HARNESS_BINDING_UNPROVEN. Two shape differences from the Claude Code binding are structural rather than stylistic and must not be smoothed over: Codex has no per-command allow/deny list at all, so its classes bind through an OS-level sandbox and an approval mode instead — the test is the outcome, not the syntax — and its sandbox does not scope READS, which leaves P2's direct-read half with no native mechanism (see that class's residual). Filling the permissions.md Codex rows with this file is not the same as clearing them: the rows now say what WOULD bind and what would not, which is what an operator needs before installing the harness, and the launch still does not happen.

classes.title: the access layer is never touched from a worker

mechanisms.detail: DECLARED: the documented sandbox confines writes to the workspace and denies privileged operations at the OS layer (Landlock/seccomp on Linux), which is a stronger mechanism than a command matcher where it applies. UNVERIFIED here: whether it actually refuses `sudo` and `systemctl` invocations, or merely fails them, has not been measured on this deployment
DECLARED: pins the approval mode explicitly so the boundary is not whatever the operator's config.toml happens to say. danger-full-access is refused by forbidden_argv_tokens

probes.note: cannot be run: the harness is not installed

classes.residual: Unmeasured. A sandbox that blocks writes is not automatically one that blocks a privileged read or a network-configuration call, and this row will say which only after the binary exists here.

classes.title: secrets are never read, never printed, never committed

mechanisms.detail: ENFORCEABLE AND NOT VENDOR-DEPENDENT: the child's environment is constructed by the launcher's own adapter from an allowlist, and credential-shaped names are refused there. This half of P2 binds on Codex exactly as it binds on Claude Code, because the launcher owns it

classes.residual: THE NAMED GAP. Codex's documented sandbox scopes WRITES and network, not READS: there is no per-path read denial equivalent to Claude Code's Read(**/*.env). So P2's direct-read half has no native Codex mechanism, and the environment allowlist plus instructions is all this descriptor can honestly claim. Closing it needs either a Codex control this descriptor's author did not find, or an already-approved isolation layer around the worker root — a decision that is the operator's and is not taken here. Until then, this class alone is enough reason for the route to refuse.

classes.title: the durable stack is never mutated, and shared infrastructure is never destroyed

mechanisms.detail: DECLARED: writes outside the workspace root are denied at the OS layer, which would cover the container-runtime and multiplexer sockets that P3's incidents ran through — including tmux kill-server, whose effect is a write to the server socket outside the workspace. UNVERIFIED: whether the socket path is in fact outside the sandbox's writable set on this host has not been measured
DECLARED: with approvals off and the sandbox on, an escalation request fails rather than prompting an absent operator

probes.note: cannot be run: the harness is not installed. Deliberately targets a private socket so that a future run of this probe cannot destroy the real multiplexer even if the binding fails

classes.residual: Unmeasured, and the tmux case in particular is a guess about socket paths rather than a reading of behaviour.

classes.title: the network is reached through named tools, not raw fetches

mechanisms.detail: DECLARED: network access is documented as disabled by default under this sandbox mode, which would close P4 STRUCTURALLY rather than by naming curl and wget — a materially stronger mechanism than the Claude Code row, and the reason this table compares outcomes rather than syntax. UNVERIFIED here

probes.note: cannot be run: the harness is not installed

classes.residual: If network is off wholesale, the positive half of P4 also needs measuring: git over https and uv/package installs must still work, or the route is bound and useless. That trade is exactly what a probe run would settle and no document can.
